title: Canine normal vitals
why_this_matters: Human vital-sign ranges do not transfer to dogs, and a resting respiratory rate above the healthy range is an early sign of trouble; only one healthy-dog respiratory rate dataset has been retrieved so far [1].

what_changes_from_human.point: In 114 apparently healthy adult dogs measured at home, the mean sleeping respiratory rate was 13 breaths/min and no dog averaged above 23; mean resting rate was 19 breaths/min [1].
Instantaneous sleeping rates above 30 breaths/min were rare (3 dogs), so a sustained rate above 30 in a sleeping or calm dog is unusual [1].

recognition: Respiratory rate: sleeping mean 13 (all dogs under 23); resting mean 19 breaths/min. Age, body weight and location did not change the sleeping rate [1].
The study measured dogs at home; hospital or field values, and dogs that are panting, excited or hot, are not covered [1].

takeaway: Dogs breathe slowly at rest (about 13 to 19 breaths per minute in healthy adults); do not judge a dog by human vital-sign ranges.

sources.citation: Rishniw M et al. 2012. Sleeping respiratory rates in apparently healthy adult dogs. Res Vet Sci.
